topic: the French WWI officer whose tactics manual got shelved before Germany invented the same thing
title: He Wrote The Tactics That Ended Trench Warfare. His Army Buried It.
description: AI-narrated commentary on a real WWI story: a French officer's own army buried the tactics manual he wrote, tactics Germany's storm troopers had already built on their own before they ever captured it. #history #wwi #shorts

hook_candidates.text: Germany's storm troopers already had these trench-breaking tactics before they ever captured the French manual that supposedly gave it to them.
What if the officer who wrote the tactics that broke trench warfare got ignored by his own side?
A wounded French captain handed his army the tactics manual that could've ended trench warfare years early, they shelved it.
Three strange facts about the manual that supposedly taught Germany how to win World War One.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the coworker who insists their brilliant idea got stolen at work, because they want to show even history's most famous 'stolen' idea might not have been stolen at all.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume Germany's storm troopers only got these tactics after they captured a French manual.
closing_comment: Laffargue's manual is the wildest part of this trench warfare story, his own army buried the exact tactics Germany figured out on its own.

sources.note: Confirms Laffargue was wounded leading the 9 May 1915 attack and wrote his infiltration-tactics pamphlet during recovery.
Confirms the German assault unit (Sturmabteilung Calsow) was formed in March 1915, before Laffargue's pamphlet was captured.
Confirms Germany captured and translated Laffargue's pamphlet in 1916, and that French command circulated it without adopting it as doctrine.
